evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.18.3: hōrologium mittam et librōs
Plin. Ep. 1.11.1: ōlim mihi nūllās epistulās mittis
terms.comment: The person in the dative or with ad: tibi mittimus, ad tē mīsī. Also “let go”: Mitte mē!, let me go.
To make someone come: medicum arcessere, to send for the doctor.

phrases.latin: hōrologium mittam et librōs, sī erit sūdum
phrases.english: I’ll send the clock and the books, if the weather is dry

phrases.latin: dē nostrō, fācunde, tibi, Juvenālis, agellō Sāturnāliciās mittimus, ecce, nucēs
phrases.english: from my own little farm, eloquent Juvenal, look, I send you nuts for the Saturnalia
you haven’t sent me a single letter for ages

sources: Lewis & Short: mitto · Lewis & Short: arcesso
